query: Consider the following context: Phonon scattering by SRO precipitates might be expected to reduce scattering times and, therefore, decrease thermal conductivity. In that context, which material can be used for lattice heat conductivity, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Aluminum (Al) alloys with a small amount of Scandium (Sc) can be used for lattice heat conductivity because the Scandium precipitates will reduce phonon scattering times, thus decreasing thermal conductivity.
generation.material_initial_state: Face-centered cubic (FCC) Aluminum (Al) alloy with a small amount of Scandium (Sc)
generation.intervention: Addition of Scandium (Sc) precipitates to the Aluminum (Al) alloy
generation.conditions: Temperature range: 300-500 K, Scandium concentration: 0.1-0.5 wt%
generation.mechanism: Phonon scattering by Scandium (Sc) precipitates, reducing mean free path and increasing phonon scattering rate
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermal conductivity reduction of 10-20% compared to pure Aluminum (Al)
generation.baseline: Pure Aluminum (Al) thermal conductivity at 300 K
generation.boundary: Scandium (Sc) concentration above 1 wt% may lead to significant changes in the alloy microstructure, affecting thermal conductivity
generation.uncertainty: The actual reduction in thermal conductivity may vary depending on the size, distribution, and morphology of the Scandium (Sc) precipitates, as well as the specific alloy composition and processing history

falsification_experiment.design: Measure thermal conductivity of Al-Sc alloys with varying Sc concentrations using a steady-state heat flow method
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured thermal conductivity reduction is less than 5% for Sc concentrations between 0.1-0.5 wt%, the hypothesis is falsified
